env.ours: x3d.threejs reader (shared with the Babylon bridge) + three.js body, bundle sha fa1672fe84a6

gaps: the frame at an interior spine point: this node (like the Library hall Extrusion) takes the Y axis along the chord spine[i+1] - spine[i-1], which is how the standard words it (Likely: read from memory of 19775-1 13.3.5, the text itself is not in the repository); X_ITE 16.6.0 takes the bisector of the two unit vectors. The two are the same for an evenly spaced spine (octagon trajectory: 1.2e-7) and differ by up to 0.017 in the 2.2 unit vase whose spine points are unevenly spaced (compared at 0.02)

solid FALSE seen from behind: X_ITE 16.6.0 lights the back face, the Babylon body draws it black (the same gap as the patch and IndexedFaceSet); the two sided swung surface here is seen from the front
no scale, orientation or caps (the NURBS nodes have none); texture coordinates run 0..1 along the profile (s) and the trajectory (t), the same numbers as X_ITE

the normals are smoothed over every shared vertex (crease angle pi, as X_ITE sets it): the shading agrees in the pictures (mean colour within 10 of 255, picture difference about 3 of 255), not per vertex
scope: triangle corners and texture coordinates come from the vertex arrays X_ITE builds (private getVertices, getMultiTexCoords) and from the mesh this reader builds; pictures are silhouette and mean colour (SwiftShader CPU raster, no tone curve); NurbsSweptSurface (a later batch) shares the extrusion code
